schema_note: No stories schema is defined by the command spec (NA-B13). This minimal deterministic schema was adopted in plan.md section 7 and recorded in planning_qa_report.json: {feature_id, schema_version, scope_of_record, epics[], stories[], slices[]}. Each slice.id equals its task file name under tasks/ without the .md extension. acceptance_criteria entries cite section-qualified ids because criteria above A90 collide two ways (NA-B05).

marker_key.rule: Every schedule, effort, duration and volume estimate is [I] with low confidence. size_class is ordinal and explicitly non-temporal; no per-slice day estimate is published (plan.md section 6.4).

stories.title: Prove the product is buildable as written before committing scope

stories.so_that: no server-dependent scope is committed against an unproven harness behaviour

stories.title: A TypeScript spine that installs once and resumes from disk

stories.title: An interview that ends with a concept, not a questionnaire

stories.title: A prompt that cannot silently lose or invent anything

stories.title: An ingest that refuses rather than half-applies
stories.as_a: ACOS owner pasting generated code back
stories.i_want: validation, quarantine and a zero-paste alternative

stories.title: Coherence by computation, enforced by lints

stories.title: One document, one renderer, one deterministic output

stories.title: A surface where everything is reachable

stories.title: Edits that are typed, atomic and undoable as one thought

stories.title: A safety net that makes experimenting cheap

stories.title: Two writers, no lost work, and a localhost that is not a doorway

stories.title: Responsive authoring where nothing is invisible

stories.title: The canvas tail, and proof that D2 works

stories.title: Swaps that never destroy copy and never ship a placeholder

stories.so_that: a swap cannot silently delete my writing or ship a fake statistic

stories.title: Art and motion in one container contract

stories.title: An export that proves it is clean

slices.title: Gate 16-A turn-boundary probe and launcher-rung decision
slices.objective: Determine whether a long-running local server survives this harness's turn boundary, and at which rung of the F1-F5 ladder.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The probe passes at least three post-turn-boundary checks and one across an eternity /clear, with the original pid still in ps at each check.
The chosen rung is recorded as ADR-01; if it is F4 or F5 the slice halts pending explicit user sign-off and records the halt.

slices.title: Generation-surface font-policy probe (60 seconds)
slices.objective: Establish whether a generation-surface artifact renders a linked web font or silently falls back, before the Step-2 prompt spec is written.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A devtools observation records whether the font file loads or is blocked, with the network entry captured as evidence.
The result is recorded as ADR-02 and the base64 embedding mandate is either confirmed or relaxed in writing.

slices.title: Build-substrate spike: framework versus plain generated HTML
slices.objective: Choose the preview and build substrate, or confirm that invariant I6 keeps the choice open, without hard-depending on any framework.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The same one-page render is produced on both candidate substrates and scored on live-editability, LOCK cleanliness and dependency surface.
ADR-03 records the outcome and states which gate-2 installer invocation it implies (NA-11).

slices.title: Process-topology spike and ADR
slices.objective: Decide single-origin proxy versus two-origin iframe plus message passing on measured evidence, not preference.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The same two-page vertical slice runs on both topologies, scored on channel LOC, preview-only screenshot achievability, HMR round-trip latency for a move op, and behaviour after killing and restarting the preview process.
ADR-04 is written and names which of I1-I6 it changes and which it leaves untouched.

slices.title: Two-build byte-reproducibility spike
slices.objective: Establish whether byte-identical two-build comparison is achievable on the selected toolchain before success criterion S4 is treated as committed.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Two clean builds are compared by sorted-path SHA-256 manifest and the result is recorded with the exact environment pinning used.
If it fails, the normalised-comparison fallback is specified with an enumerated, individually justified exception set, and the slice records that D3's proof is weakened and sign-off is required.

slices.title: Channel-fidelity, output-ceiling, latency and licence battery
slices.objective: Measure the hand-carry channel's real behaviour and re-verify every adopted dependency licence against its actual licence file, plus the non-blocking subagent-availability probe.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Copy-paste fidelity is tested across all three paste paths (rendered view, per-block copy control, conversation export) and the fenced-block contract is confirmed or revised.
An empirical output ceiling is measured from real artifacts; no published figure is used (one referenced model name in published guides appears fabricated).
Every adopted dependency's licence is re-verified against the actual LICENSE file at pin time and the result recorded per dependency.
The subagent-availability probe result is recorded as ADR-06 and is explicitly not a v1 blocker.

slices.title: Thin router SKILL.md with the mandatory Confirmation Gate
slices.objective: Ship a router skill whose frontmatter is exactly as specified and whose Phase 0 refuses to write anything before an explicit human confirmation.

slices.title: Port the in-estate Python server to server.ts (the TypeScript spine)
slices.objective: Establish the TypeScript spine as the first code written, serving the route contract on the fixed loopback port with state.json at boot.

acceptance_criteria.statement: state.json carries {phase, step, awaiting, nextAction, port, pid, url, sessionId} at boot and regenerate-if-stale runs on startup.

slices.title: Symlink installer, project config, session tree, nested git repo, selftest harness
slices.objective: Make installation drift-proof and every session resumable, versioned and self-testable from the first run.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The session tree matches the specified directory layout exactly, with an ACTIVE marker written at init and a config snapshot in audit/.

slices.title: Warm-start scan and asset-library detection
slices.objective: Offer any reusable prior system inside the first three exchanges and determine, early, whether the artwork category is real for this project.

slices.title: System/identity split, negative constraints and mined-source pre-fill
slices.objective: Carry forward what is reusable and deliberately exclude what is identity, injecting prior identities as negative constraints.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The carried set and the excluded set match the specified split exactly, item for item, and are recorded in session.json.
Prior hue anchors and type pairings appear in the Step-2 prompt as explicit negative constraints unless the sibling-site question was answered yes.

slices.title: The 90-question interview bank with its ID grammar
slices.objective: Author the bank as a reference file with stable ids, correct tier labels and no id collisions with the tier notation.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The bank contains 90 questions [V] and a mechanical row count in the selftest asserts it.
The ten taste questions are TS1-TS10; a grep proves no question id matches ^T[0-9] (which would collide with tier labels and break A4).

slices.title: Interview engine: tiers, waves, real branch map, policy questions, instrumentation
slices.objective: Deliver the interview in hard-gated waves with honest tier semantics, a branch map that matches the bank, and elapsed-time instrumentation from day one.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Recorded as unachievable as written: the bank's own estimate is 45-55 Tier-1 questions in fast mode (NA-01). The slice implements the fast-mode path and records the measured count rather than asserting compliance.
Every Tier-1 'I don't know / surprise me' answer records a stated concrete default value with source skill-default, and never a null.
The branch map is asserted in the selftest: C6 gates B4 and conditionally D8; L1 prunes L2-L4; G1 with G0 prunes G2 but not G3; D4 prunes nothing; no-forms skips D7 and D11.
The audience-access-needs answer can only tighten a gate threshold; a selftest asserts no code path loosens one.

slices.title: Concept-document synthesis, inline, with the refusal requirement
slices.objective: Turn answers into a 200-300 word concept the human recognises, and refuse to advance without a stated refusal.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The synthesis runs inline in the main session against the role prompt using only already-declared tools; no subagent call exists on this path.
answers.json is question-ID-keyed and tier-tagged with source in {asked, pre-filled, inferred-default, skill-default} plus an override flag.

slices.title: Font catalog with pre-subsetted cuts, and the per-session snapshot
slices.objective: Build a skill-owned font catalog whose base64 cuts are computed locally ahead of time, and pin a hash-stamped copy per session.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Every catalog entry carries familyId, classification, foundry, licence source URL, fileHash, glyphCoverage and pre-subsetted latin cuts; a missing licence class fails the build.
A session snapshot is written at Step-2 start and its hash is compared at prompt emission, so a mid-run library refresh cannot change what the session is judging.

slices.title: Mechanical token manifest and the Stage-A capsule prompt
slices.objective: Emit a frozen token-name manifest generated mechanically from the inventory, and a Stage-A prompt that is greppably complete and traceable to interview ids.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The token manifest is generated from the inventory item list (names only, no values) and is re-pasted verbatim into every chunk; a diff proves byte equality across chunks.
Capsules are over-generated, machine pre-filtered on the self-audit fields, then cut by the user; any relaxation of the direction floor is written to session.json as a signed-off deviation.

slices.title: Stage-B prompt, envelope manifest, terminator and runtime chunk computation
slices.objective: Make truncation detectable by construction and size chunks from measured artifacts rather than any published ceiling.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The envelope declares the file list, per-file line counts, sha256 prefixes, smallest-first ordering and a per-run random terminator.
Chunk sizes are computed from measured artifact sizes at runtime; a grep proves no published ceiling constant exists in the code.
The usage-tier cost of a two-stage run across N directions is surfaced to the user before the first chunk is emitted.

slices.title: Tolerant FILE-block parser with envelope validation and no partial writes
slices.objective: Ingest a complete chunk in one paste, and fail a truncated chunk loudly without writing a partial system.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A deliberately truncated fixture leaves zero files written under the system directory, proven by a directory diff before and after.

slices.title: AST-resolving validator, quarantine, deterministic re-verification and substitution
slices.objective: Treat the paste as untrusted input: resolve bindings through an AST, fail closed on the undecidable, and re-verify every claimed contrast and font.

acceptance_criteria.statement: An imported component using window["fe"+"tch"](...) is quarantined by the AST validator, and a parse failure quarantines rather than passes.
The anti-slop lint runs as a hard gate on the generated design-system JSON before the human sees any menu of choices.

slices.title: Local Regeneration Mode: the zero-paste path
slices.objective: Make the web hop a UX preference rather than a technical dependency by producing an identical-format bundle with zero pastes.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The bundle produced locally passes the identical validator path used for pasted bundles, proven by running the same validator binary on both fixtures.

slices.title: Token compiler: DTCG JSON, forge YAML, custom properties and theme layer
slices.objective: Emit both consumers from one importer and make derived values structurally un-pickable.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Font fallback metrics are emitted as a derived token family computed from the real selected font binary, and carry pickable false.
Every in-direction-repickable row ships a per-direction validity list; a row that cannot supply one is demoted to direction-slot by the compiler, not by a human.

slices.title: Flat variable layer per direction change, machine-owned stylesheet, extract-override
slices.objective: Keep drag-time cost off the token graph and give hand-tuning one sanctioned door.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The custom-property set is compiled to a flat layer exactly once per direction change; an instrumentation counter proves zero re-resolutions during a drag.
The compiled stylesheet carries a do-not-hand-edit banner and extract-override produces a valid override file that survives regeneration.

slices.title: The versioned coherence-lint set, run at ingest and at LOCK
slices.objective: Replace an unstable lint count with a versioned set whose required members are named, including logical-properties-only.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A grep over generated CSS returns zero physical-direction declarations (left, right, top, bottom, margin-left, text-align: left) at ingest and at LOCK.
The lint set carries a version number; gates cite the version and never a count (NA-05).

slices.title: Document schema and canonical serialisation
slices.objective: Define the scene graph as per-page documents plus a project record, serialised canonically so a re-serialise is always a zero diff.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Re-serialising every doc-owned JSON file produces a zero diff; a file with collapsed arrays or reordered keys fails the pre-commit hook and purity gate 8.
A doc containing an upward override key is rejected by the schema validator with a message naming the desktop-down rule.
No file named layout.json is created anywhere; the canonical names are used throughout (NA-07).
Absent optional keys are omitted entirely rather than written null, so the key-presence override test stays valid.

slices.title: Pure, total renderer with the normative resolution policy
slices.objective: Render from documents with one code path for the design surface and for LOCK, and define exactly what happens when a reference does not resolve.

acceptance_criteria.statement: An unknown component id opens the editor read-only in a migration-required state and refuses both generate and LOCK, naming every affected node and page.
An unknown variant falls back to the direction's canonical variant, writes a migration flag, and blocks LOCK until acknowledged.
A removed slot moves its content to the node's orphan store; no migration path deletes content.
The DOM is never serialised back into the document; a grep proves no reverse-parse code path exists.

slices.title: Breakpoint vocabulary and the desktop-down cascade compiler
slices.objective: Make one breakpoint vocabulary normative across switcher, cascade, free-position rules, save format and gates.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A node with a base entry and no small-key entry compiles to grid-column: 1 / -1 inside the small media query, and the emitted rule order is base, then md, then sm.
No emitted rule uses !important to win the cascade; ordering alone decides.

slices.title: Determinism contract: six hazards designed out
slices.objective: Make generation a pure function of documents, system lock and generator version, so verify can be trusted.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Every generated file carries the generated marker, document hash, system-lock hash and generator version, and contains no timestamp.
Binary assets are hash-compared using their recorded encoder record and are never re-encoded during verification.
A grep proves generate-time code reads no clock, no network, no random source, no environment and no path outside the session root.

slices.title: DEMO 1 - interview to prompt to ingest to one direction rendered static
slices.objective: Prove end to end that a conversation becomes a coherent, licence-clean design system and a page a human can look at.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A single recorded run produces answers.json, concept.md, both prompt stages, an ingested system and a rendered static page, with screenshots at 390 and 1280 captured at pinned device heights.

slices.title: Three-pane editor shell with the out-of-iframe overlay and same-origin preview
slices.objective: Stand up the editing surface with zero DOM injection for hit-testing and a preview that can be captured without chrome.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Selection overlay and handles are drawn outside the iframe with pointer-events none; a grep proves no injected hit-test node is added to the page tree.
The preview is a same-origin iframe, and device heights are pinned with the measured iframe height asserted whenever the page contains a viewport-unit rule.

slices.title: Navigator/layers tree and three-way selection parity
slices.objective: Guarantee everything is reachable, including what canvas clicking provably cannot reach.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A fixture containing a zero-height wrapper, a fully covered element, a pointer-events-none decoration and an empty slot is fully selectable from the tree, and each case is recorded.

slices.title: Typed-op engine, autosave, op log and transactional undo
slices.objective: Make every edit a validated typed op applied atomically by the single writer, with one command stack over the document.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The browser never sends a raw patch or a file path; a request carrying either is rejected with 400 and the rejection is logged.
Writes are atomic (write-temp then rename) and every applied op appends op, patch and inverse to the op log.
A continuous drag coalesces into exactly one undo entry.

slices.title: Inline plaintext-only text editing
slices.objective: Let the human edit copy in place without source-app markup surviving into the type system.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Pasting rich text from a word processor into any editable node yields plain text only, proven by inspecting the stored content value.
Inline editing is available on the named text node classes (headings, eyebrows, buttons, nav items, labels, stat numbers) and each edit commits as a typed op.

slices.title: Image replace, focal point, blocking alt gate and auto-recompression
slices.objective: Make image handling preserve composition and make missing alt text impossible to place, not merely impossible to ship.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Replacing an image preserves container size, crop and position; cropping uses a single draggable focal point, never a crop rectangle.
Every derived image records encoder, encoder version, settings hash and output hash in the asset manifest.

slices.title: Section reorder, duplicate, copy/paste with overrides, and element freeze
slices.objective: Give the structural edits that precede the canvas, without losing breakpoint overrides or overloading the word lock.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Copy-paste and duplicate round-trip a fragment including every breakpoint override, proven by a document diff of the pasted subtree.
A grep over all user-visible strings proves the element-level protection verb is Freeze and the word Lock is never used for it.
A frozen node rejects move, resize, swap, reorder and delete, and says why.

slices.title: Named snapshots, save-as-variation and the recovery bin
slices.objective: Make experimenting cheap and deletion non-destructive, with a recovery path independent of undo.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A deleted subtree is restorable in place after ten subsequent unrelated edits, without reverting those edits.
Autosave stores small document diffs through the server; a grep proves no base64 blob is written to browser storage.
Save-as-variation forks the document set without mutating the source, proven by unchanged source hashes.

slices.title: Page-scoped ops (Branch A+), per-page SEO, preview mode and the Design Health HUD
slices.objective: Ship page-scoped operations and per-page metadata now so multi-page is a later feature rather than a later migration, plus one honest health surface.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The asset manager, page manager, per-page SEO fields and inline text editing each complete successfully against the write allowlist with no path outside the table written.
Every op is page-scoped and the project record carries a pages array of length one under Branch A+ (NA-B01); the multi-page manager UI and global regions are explicitly out of scope for v1.
The health pill shows three dots, a page-weight bar and a projected largest-contentful-paint from a live performance observer entry, and is the only surfacing channel for advisory findings.

slices.title: The eight-control local-server security posture
slices.objective: Treat localhost as a hostile boundary: bind, origin, exact CORS, bearer token, pinned host settings, idle shutdown, Host validation and security headers.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A bootstrap GET carrying a foreign Host header is rejected before any response body is produced; the same GET with a loopback Host succeeds.
The bearer token file is mode 0600 and never appears in any committed file or log.
Idle shutdown fires after the configured window and is recorded in the event log.
Any hook the skill registers is fail-open and is removed at close; a forced hook error still allows the tool call.

slices.title: Hash-journal reconciliation, 409 concurrency, process lock and tab claim
slices.objective: Make silent work loss impossible in either direction, with reconciliation as the authoritative mechanism rather than the guard hook.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A doc-owned file written out of band by a shell heredoc while the editor holds the lock is detected before the next save, the divergent version is preserved under the conflicts directory, and neither version is silently overwritten.
If the file-watch mechanism is unavailable the editor falls back to a hash re-check before every save and on window focus, and says so in the status bar; a silently degraded detector fails the slice.
A second browser tab is read-only, and the claim is carried over the event stream.

slices.title: Ownership guard with stated limits, the sanctioned agent write path, and the inbox
slices.objective: Give the agent a legal write path so the ownership rule is followed rather than routed around, and keep one validation path for both writers.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Amended to the write-allowlist table (NA-B15): the server writes only the allowlisted path shapes, verified by realpath plus prefix assertion, and a symlinked path is rejected.
A typed op whose derived patch targets the system-lock pointer is rejected with 400, whichever op produced it.
The command-line write path applies the same typed op through the same server, and starts a headless server when none is running, so the agent path never depends on a browser being open.
The guard's limits are documented in the skill instructions: it is a heuristic defeatable by indirection, and reconciliation is the authoritative mechanism.

slices.title: DEMO 2 - a live editable surface proven across at least two turn boundaries
slices.objective: Prove the editor premise holds in this harness, with survival evidence rather than a same-turn response.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Inline text edit, section reorder, variant swap and autosave are demonstrated in one session, and the server answers a health check in a separate tool call after each of at least two turn boundaries with the original pid alive.
The demo recording notes which launcher rung was in use, because that is the fact worth carrying into the estate's memory.

slices.title: Gridline overlay derived from computed styles
slices.objective: Paint the real resolved grid tracks as the snap target, in the out-of-iframe overlay so they vanish at LOCK by construction.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The overlay is never a hand-authored decorative grid; a test proves the painted track positions equal the computed template columns for three different section archetypes.
A capture of the preview with the overlay active contains zero overlay pixels, because the overlay lives outside the iframe.

slices.title: Snap engine with prioritised target classes and zoom-scaled tolerance
slices.objective: Snap to the four target classes in priority order with tolerance divided by zoom, using interval indexes rather than per-frame scans.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Two one-dimensional interval indexes per section are built once per layout change; a counter proves no full sibling scan happens per pointer move.
Priority order is asserted by test: grid lines beat sibling edges and centres, which beat section padding and content rails, which beat spacing-scale increments.

slices.title: Drag-to-place writing grid integers, with the normative drop algorithm
slices.objective: Implement the full normative drop algorithm including row derivation, span preservation, displace-down occupancy with ghost preview, re-parenting and the three legal rejections.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Nine acceptance branches are covered by tests: column derivation, row derivation, span preservation with clamping shown before commit, displace-down cascade with ghost preview, art-container z-order resolution, opt-in overlap with a counter, cross-section re-parenting with no auto-compaction, boundary-zone append, and the three rejection cases with an inline message rather than a silent clamp.
Persisted placement is integers only; a grep proves no pixel coordinate is ever written to a document.

slices.title: Span resize, padding/gap handles on the scale, and smart guides
slices.objective: Make direct manipulation teach the token system rather than erode it, with token-named readouts and fluid-consequence feedback.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Span resize commits whole cells and displays a fraction-and-percentage readout during the drag.
Padding and gap handles snap only to discrete spacing-scale steps; an attempt to commit an off-scale value is impossible by construction, not merely warned about.
Alignment guides show live distance labels and an equal-spacing indicator appears when three or more siblings match.

slices.title: Keyboard parity for every drag, three verbs, and editor target size
slices.objective: Satisfy the two accessibility criteria that apply to the tool itself, and keep the anchor vocabulary to exactly three verbs.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Arrow moves one cell, shift-arrow changes span by one, tab walks siblings, and a select-then-click-destination path exists for every drag operation.
The anchor control exposes exactly three verbs (align to, space above/below over the scale, order among siblings) and no fourth appears in the UI.
A live bounding-rect check runs on render over all editor chrome and reports any control below the minimum target size with its documented exception, if any.

slices.title: Per-breakpoint override cascade, pre-commit chip and overridden-here dots
slices.objective: Make invisible overrides visible and make every breakpoint-scoped edit announce its blast radius before it commits.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The breakpoint indicator is structurally prominent chrome, not a dropdown; the active key is also persisted in session UI state.
Every overridden property shows a dot with one-click reset to inherited, and the panel lists every breakpoint-specific value for the selected node.
Override accumulation escalates at the recorded starting thresholds and the counts land in the gate report; the thresholds are read from the project record, not hardcoded.

slices.title: Reading-order invariant, focusable-node hard block and numbered mobile stack preview
slices.objective: Guarantee document order is reading order, and make any mobile reordering visible before it is committed.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Visual order is achieved only by grid placement; a test proves no editor path reorders the document tree to achieve a visual effect.
An order override on a focusable node is refused outright with an explanation; on a non-focusable node it warns and raises a persistent chip.
Any commit that changes mobile stacking first renders a numbered list preview of the resulting top-to-bottom sequence.

slices.title: Free-position escape hatch: anchored offset, authored flow fallback, demotion and lock gate
slices.objective: Ship the escape hatch narrowly: parent or grid-cell anchors only, with reserved space, an authored fallback, a visible counter and a hard lock gate.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Auto-demotion fires at the recorded demotion width; note NA-06 - the demotion trigger and the small media-query boundary are NOT the same number, and the criterion text must be read against the project record value.
Anchors are restricted to parent or grid line/cell; sibling anchoring is absent from the schema, not merely hidden in the UI (the compile strategy behind it is unprototyped).
Every free-position drop writes an authored flow fallback that is independently editable in the navigator, and drops z-stacking at the small key unless the fallback carries an explicit z.
The per-section cap is enforced with a visible counter, and the locked export contains no runtime positioning script.

slices.title: Canvas tail: zoom/pan, rulers, guides, marquee multi-select, align and distribute
slices.objective: Deliver the tail of the canvas if budget allows, knowing it is the first scope traded back out.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Zoom spans the documented range with tolerance divided by zoom and space-drag panning; guides are stored as fractions, not pixels.
Section archetypes ship as template areas per direction, and dragging a block off its area promotes THAT BLOCK ONLY to explicit integer placement on the same grid.
This slice is explicitly first in the trade-back-out order; if it is dropped, the drop is recorded rather than silently omitted.

slices.title: DEMO 3 - gridlines, constraint drag, per-breakpoint overrides and the free-position hatch
slices.objective: Exercise the settled constraint-layout decision for the first time and either survive or diagnose the friction risk it carries.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The recorded session includes the friction test: move a hero headline up by one spacing step using each of the three verbs and the keyboard path, and record whether the tool fought the user.
Elapsed effort for the three placement sub-slices is recorded, because it is the only path from inference to a defensible schedule number (NA-B10).

slices.title: Typed slot contracts, superset-only swaps, content orphanage and lock-blocking placeholders
slices.objective: Make a variant swap incapable of destroying hand-written copy and incapable of shipping an unfilled placeholder.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The bar offers only superset-or-exact contract matches and states the slot delta in words before the swap is applied.
Cross-direction swaps are absent from v1 by construction; the coherence-debt ledger exists but has no cross-direction producer.

slices.title: Hand-authored variant-axis schema
slices.objective: Define structural distinctness machine-checkably, per component, so the variant budget stays finite.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Every component in the v1 set declares an axis vector; a selftest asserts full coverage of the v1 target of 88 rows (NA-B08).

Computed axes (size, theme, density, state, icon slot, semantic colour) are excluded from the variant budget by construction, and a test proves two variants differing only on a computed axis are treated as the same variant.

slices.title: Deterministic, lazy, append-only variant generator with the indistinguishability rule
slices.objective: Generate variants from tokens with no model call, only on first panel open, and never offer two the eye cannot tell apart.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The generator is a pure function of the direction's tokens and the axis schema; a grep proves no model call and no subagent write exists on this path.
Variants are generated on first open of a family panel only, cached per direction, and never generated for unused families; an instrumentation counter proves it.
Indices are append-only and collision-free across repeated generation rounds.

slices.title: One container contract for art and motion, with the pause affordance field
slices.objective: Implement the container contract and its seven rules so unpausable or unreduced motion is structurally unbuildable.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Validation fails a motion-capable container with no reduced-motion sibling reference, and fails an autoplay video container that is not muted.
Animation inside a container can only touch transform, opacity and filter; a test proves a rule touching grid placement, width or height is rejected.
The pause affordance field exists on the contract and a container that needs one and lacks it cannot be constructed.
Motion is disabled in edit mode and judged in preview mode; the limitation is stated in the UI rather than worked around (R14 has no known mitigation).

slices.title: Lane A - code-drawn, token-parameterised artwork that re-skins with the direction
slices.objective: Deliver the artwork lane that is actually available from the generation channel, and make it move with the hue anchors.

slices.title: Lane B ingestion, asset manifest, affinity filter chips, Lane C runbook and the honest warning
slices.objective: Ingest a real asset library with licence classes and affinity tags, and tell the user the truth at interview time when there is none.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Every ingested asset lands in the manifest with a licence class, a direction-affinity tag set and a file hash; an asset without a licence class fails ingestion.
The asset pane filters by direction affinity with chips; presenting twenty artworks without chips is treated as a defect.
The external-raster runbook exists as a document and its output ingests through the same manifest path; no external generation is invoked by the skill in v1.
A project with no asset library receives an explicit warning at interview time, before a design system the pipeline cannot fully deliver is generated.

slices.title: More variants and more like this
slices.objective: Give the two cheapest regeneration gears: extend the set, or explore the neighbourhood of something already approved.

acceptance_criteria.statement: More variants appends the next N from the current highest index with no collisions; more like this appends exactly five deterministic neighbours of the approved variant.
Both paths respect the indistinguishability rule against everything already offered in the same bar.

slices.title: Per-section notes driving scoped inline regeneration as one undo step
slices.objective: Ship the middle gear between swapping one variant and regenerating everything, executed inline with no second hand-carry.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A note attached to a section regenerates that section only; a document diff proves no other section changed.
The regeneration runs inline through the local path, never a second hand-carry, and every run appends to the regeneration log.
Section notes are stripped from published output at LOCK.

slices.title: Redesign as a fork, reviewed application, and the migration report
slices.objective: Make a new direction a reviewed operation that never silently substitutes and never silently drops a node.

acceptance_criteria.statement: After importing a new direction every affected node carries a migration flag, the editor lists them, LOCK is refused until they are acknowledged, and the migration report names every changed reference.
Migration snapshots the documents before touching anything, shows a plan with counts before applying, and applies through the same typed-op path so every change is individually undoable.
Unmappable nodes are listed explicitly for human resolution; a test proves no node is dropped silently.
Variant matching is canonical fallback only in v1; semantic slot-signature matching is absent (NA-B04).
Redesign forks via save-as-variation and does not replace in place.

slices.title: Whitelisted registry components: table, embed and form
slices.objective: Ship the narrow custom-component registry against the direction's tokens, with a real placement path.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Only the four whitelisted kinds can be inserted; anything else is refused with a message naming the v1 scope.
Each kind has a working insertion path in the editor, because shipping a capability with no insertion path silently cuts it; this row and the chart-data field carry a sign-off note.
The inline-authored path runs the full coherence lint set before acceptance and registers through the custom-slot contract that enforces token usage.

slices.title: Build-time SVG charts with dataviz sub-tokens and two shipped data states
slices.objective: Make charts read as one system with the site, colourblind-safe in both schemes, and ship no chart runtime.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Charts are emitted as build-time SVG with at most four mark types; a grep proves no chart runtime ships in the published tree.
Colour ramps are derived from the direction's colour anchors and validated colourblind-safe in both light and dark schemes.
Only the empty and single-data-point states ship; loading and error states exist as editor-only previews labelled as not shown to visitors.
The chrome kit treatments are applied consistently across all mark types, which is what makes a site's charts read as one system.

slices.title: Inline-authored components, coherence debt, the signature-moment rule and third-party marks
slices.objective: Allow bespoke work through one audited door, record what it costs in coherence, and never redraw a third-party mark.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The opaque custom-code-block container is absent from v1 by construction and is recorded as the v2 home of the quality ceiling.
The signature moment is 2-3 bespoke concept candidates per direction, and a lint flags a second signature moment.
Accepted off-system values are written to the coherence-debt ledger with a reason.

slices.title: Structured gate verdicts and the four severity tiers
slices.objective: Give every gate one shape - measured value, threshold, verdict, evidence reference - and never throw on a normal fail.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Every gate returns a structured verdict; a forced failure returns a verdict rather than an exception, and an inconclusive verdict blocks exactly like a fail.
Tier semantics are enforced in code: tier zero blocks the individual edit, tier one blocks LOCK only, tier two is advisory and batched into the health pill, tier three is silent.
Repeated violations collapse into one counted badge rather than a stream.

slices.title: Live checks: scoped, sub-100ms, drop and mouseup only
slices.objective: Run the live half of the gate suite without ever fighting the drag, including the running motion-concurrency counter.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Live checks fire on drop and mouseup only; an instrumentation trace proves zero checks run mid-drag or per frame, and the scoped run stays under the latency budget on the reference fixture.
Contrast is recomputed for every touched pair in both the standing ratio and the advisory perceptual measure; the standing ratio is the gate.
The motion-concurrency counter accumulates visibly turn by turn rather than surfacing at LOCK; the anti-slop lint appears here only as a dismissible advisory, never as a block.

slices.title: Capture wrapper with the inherited wait recipe and device-height pinning
slices.objective: Produce captures that are valid evidence, especially for viewport-height layouts, with zero npm dependencies.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Capture uses the browser command line with no package dependency and asserts a non-empty output file.

The wait recipe is implemented in TypeScript: navigate rather than set content, network idle with a load fallback, strip lazy-loading attributes, fonts-ready plus per-image decode, and a deferred-style settle.

Any capture judging a viewport-height layout pins both the window and the preview frame to a real device size and asserts the measured frame height; full-page tall captures are labelled content-review-only.
Fonts-ready is awaited before any bounding-rect measurement in both the editor and the capture path.

slices.title: LOCK as a re-render, with five layered editor-absence mechanisms
slices.objective: Build the published tree by re-rendering with the editor flag false, never by copying and stripping.

acceptance_criteria.statement: All five absence mechanisms exist: separate configs, commands and output directories; dev-only injection gated on the build command; toolbar-class chrome that cannot leak; the design flag explicitly defined false in the publish config; and a post-build scrub that then asserts.
LOCK strips the recovery bin, freeze flags, section notes and asset-pane state from published output while the asset manifest stays in the project and in the evidence bundle.

slices.title: The eight purity gates, with isolated two-build comparison
slices.objective: Prove the published tree is clean rather than claim it, and run the two-build comparison without touching the live dependency tree.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A grep for design-time origins across the published tree returns zero matches, including inside srcset, inline style, stylesheet url() and structured data.
Gate two runs from a clean worktree with its own dependency tree; the live manifest, lockfile and dependencies are unmodified afterwards and a concurrently running design server is unaffected.
There are eight gates, not five (NA-03); gate six fails with the node list rather than a count; gate eight re-serialises every document and requires a zero diff.
Gate two above the escalation budget demotes to CI-only with a recorded waiver in the gate report, never a silent skip.

slices.title: The 32-check ordered lock-time checklist
slices.objective: Run all 32 checks cheapest-and-most-foundational first, including the four lettered insertions and their build prerequisites.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Recorded as inconsistent with the canonical performance threshold (NA-16): it omits the interaction metric. The gate implements the canonical statement and the criterion text is flagged for amendment.
Recorded as inconsistent with the canonical pre-load transfer range (NA-16). The gate implements the canonical range.
The checklist contains 32 checks including motion-concurrency caps, skip-link presence and first tab order, the pause affordance, and asset-reference resolution (NA-04).
Licence completeness and reference resolution are two separate gates; a hallucinated asset path fails the second even though it passes the first.

slices.title: Snapshots, lock manifest, git tag, non-mutating LOCK and the unlock path
slices.objective: Make LOCK reversible and hand-edits inside the exported tree detectable rather than silently overwritten.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Amended to restore the system lock and content alongside the documents.

The snapshot contains every document, the project record, content, the system lock, the asset manifest, the distribution hash manifest, the scrub output, the lock manifest and the gate report; the built tree is excluded because it is reproducible.
Restoring an older lock stops and prints the migrate command when library files no longer hash-match the restored system lock, rather than opening a half-resolved project.

slices.title: Automated publish with an honest runbook fallback
slices.objective: Commit automated deploy as the v1 behaviour and record plainly when the fallback means the site is locked but not published.

acceptance_criteria.statement: After a one-time credential setup, lock-and-publish runs the static deploy non-interactively and records the publish path used.
With no valid credential, the run emits a runbook and records that the site is locked but NOT published; the fallback does not satisfy the locked-and-published exit criterion (NA-09).
This commitment carries an unsigned sign-off row and the slice records that fact rather than assuming approval.

slices.title: The licence-and-evidence bundle with fixed disclosure wording
slices.objective: Make the bundle the deliverable: every licence, every measured gate value, the direction tour, and a claim ceiling that is never exceeded.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A grep over the bundle and all product copy returns zero conformance claims (compliant, conformant, certified).

The direction tour is rendered from the tour log including every heat's pick and stated reason, and the reference triangulation records at least three abstracted references per direction with a regeneration trigger above the overlap threshold.
A one-line verdict is mirrored into the framework evidence directory.

slices.title: DEMO 4 - locked, published, evidence-complete
slices.objective: Demonstrate the full exit condition: a locked site with proof of purity, published, with a complete bundle.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Or the signed-off normalised-comparison fallback, recorded as weakening the export proof.
One recorded run produces a locked tree passing all eight purity gates and all tier-one lock checks, a publish record, and a bundle with zero missing licence classes.

slices.title: Resume from disk and re-attach rather than relaunch
slices.objective: Reconstruct the pipeline phase from on-disk state alone and survive a context reset without restarting a live server.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The resume path reads the frontier from populated directories and passed gates; a test proves no branch depends on conversation memory.
After a context clear, the resume text instructs re-attaching to the fixed port through the server state file and never instructs a relaunch.

slices.title: verify and doctor
slices.objective: Ship the two diagnostics that keep the drift guarantee real and name month-six rot before it is fatal.

acceptance_criteria.statement: verify regenerates to a temporary directory, diffs text files, hash-compares binaries separately and re-serialises every document to canonical form.
doctor reports hash mismatches, orphaned overrides and stale locks, and escalates override accumulation at the thresholds read from the project record.
A false-positive verify is treated as a defect of the highest severity, because a verify users learn to ignore removes the guarantee while appearing to keep it.

slices.title: Gotchas reference, provenance and do-not-hand-edit banners
slices.objective: Write down the harness facts that cost time, and make generated files say what to edit instead.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The gotchas reference carries every harness fact: cwd resets between shell calls, the missing timeout binary yielding empty output rather than an error, explicit browser invocation for previews, case-insensitive sibling directory names, and destructive-command scoring.
The generation RESULT is persisted as the artifact of record and the prompt is stored for provenance only; a grep proves no code path re-derives a system from a stored prompt.
Durable artifacts live outside the framework state directory that session cleanup touches.

slices.title: Acceptance-criteria sweep with the collision handled
slices.objective: Map all 90 criteria to a gate, a script or an observable behaviour, and cite the unstable ones section-qualified.

acceptance_criteria.statement: All 90 criteria are mapped with a named verification method, and the mapping is machine-checkable against this stories file.
Criteria above ninety are cited section-qualified because two disjoint sets share the same numbers; the renumbering recommendation is recorded (NA-B05, NA-19).
The three criteria recorded as inconsistent with their own canonical statements (the answered-question cap and the two performance rows) are reported as amendments owed, not silently satisfied.

slices.title: Selftest at full assertion pass and per-slice evidence bundles
slices.objective: Make the release claim testable and make every slice's evidence reproducible from disk.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Every slice's evidence bundle exists under the framework evidence path with all seven sections present.

slices.title: Agent-metrics scaffolding and the learning-capture loop
slices.objective: Define the performance formulas and their logging locations, and lift the run's learnings into the estate.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The metrics document defines story points delivered, quality-adjusted productivity, token efficiency ratio and the universal score, names each input's source, and computes nothing.
Instrumentation points at the existing agent-completions log plus per-slice evidence bundles.
Every slice in this feature has non-empty Dev Learnings and QA Learnings; a slice with empty learnings is reported as not Done.
The three named learning obligations are captured: the passing launcher rung, the measured canvas sub-slice effort, and every source contradiction found by reading two sections against each other.
